args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), checkout-api failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging before it was promoted. I rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and why it was promoted even though staging was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running v2.3.1, which was failing health checks with about an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. The service now passes health checks in all three regions, with an error rate of about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) covers the failure, the rollback and the recovery. Opening it paged the on-call engineer.

The deployment history also shows that v2.3.1's release candidate was already unhealthy in staging before it went to production. I added that to the incident as a follow-up, along with finding out why v2.3.1 failed.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
